paragraphs.text: Skeleton placeholder. Research CHFA Round One and Round Two Housing Tax Credit award announcements (2022-2026) for any City of Steamboat Springs project awards or denials. The Affordable Ownership Need screening module recommends Rental + ownership mix for City of Steamboat Springs. It classifies rental pressure as Very High, ownership pressure as Very High, and identifies 850 moderate-income renter households as the ownership-fit base.

The same screening run counts 1,042 renter households and 1,296 owner households as cost-burdened. This is a screening estimate only; verify local prices, financing assumptions, assistance programs, household size, and local deed-restriction policy before using it for a project decision.

The metric digest ranks City of Steamboat Springs at #8 with an overall housing-need score of 85.7. It identifies 306 deeply affordable units missing at <=30% AMI. The deep-affordability gap rate is 73.6% of <=30% AMI households. 61.4% of renter households are cost burdened, and 0.8% of occupied households are overcrowded.
Market and supply context: the digest reports a ZHVI market estimate of $1,322,059 and median gross rent of $2,017. 32.8% of households rent, and 36.8% of the housing stock is multifamily.

Demographics and demand: the population metric is 13,433. LEHD-based commuting signals show 6,519 in-commuters and a commute ratio of 57.5%. The digest's county-context projection shows 792 future units needed over 20 years, so that projection should be read as county context rather than a place trend.
Opportunity context: the digest gives an opportunity score of 79.6 and a walkability score of 36.5. These are current digest levels, not trends.

Economic and service-worker context: the digest reports a workforce-housing pressure score of 77.7. A worker earning the containing county's LEHD earnings-bin wage estimate faces an ownership affordability gap of $294,815 and a rent affordability gap of $53,180. The county-context service-sector employment share is 36.8%, and county-context ACS cohorts show median gross rent changed 112.6% from 2009 to 2024 while median household income changed 47.1%. These county-context figures are economic context, not place-level sector or wage observations.
